negative_findings.description: Repeated searches in English and Slovak for a global core-banking / digital-banking vendor case study naming a Slovak bank (Temenos, Finastra, Comarch, Backbase, Worldline, NCR, Diebold) returned no vendor customer-story page naming Tatra banka, Slovenska sporitelna, VUB or 365.bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic bank-profile and ranking pages surfaced; no vendor-hosted case study was located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Global vendors are the likeliest holders of large compliance-platform contracts at SK systemic banks; absence of findable case studies means their SK wins must be pursued via group-parent (Erste, Intesa, RBI) newsrooms and vendor press-release archives rather than country case studies.

negative_findings.description: No public announcement was found of an AML/KYC platform vendor selection by Tatra banka, Slovenska sporitelna or VUB in 2025-2026, in either Slovak or English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned regulatory background, bank profitability coverage and generic AML-vendor listicles, but no named bank-vendor AML/KYC deal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML/KYC is a core compliance-spend category for this cell; if such deals are systematically unannounced, the cell must rely on onboarding/identity vendors (Softec, NFQES) and group-level announcements as proxies.

negative_findings.description: No private-bank RFP/tender publication channel was found for SK banks outside public procurement portals — no bank-hosted 'supplier portal', 'dodávatelia' or 'obstarávanie' page surfaced for the systemic private banks in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for supplier/tender pages on bank domains produced nothing; the assumption that SK private-bank buying is unpublished appears to hold.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: vendor-side publication is the only practical route, so collection weight should sit on vendor reference pages and press wires, not on buyer-side pages.

negative_findings.description: For payment-processing and card-scheme suppliers to SK banks (e.g. processors, ATM/POS estates, instant-payments infrastructure), no vendor page naming an SK bank was located; only journalistic coverage of the joint instant-payments programme.
negative_findings.result_summary: Instant-payments programme by Tatra banka, VUB and Slovenska sporitelna is documented in trade press, but the implementing vendor is not named in sources found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payments infrastructure is deadline-driven (Instant Payments Regulation) and a major spend category; the implementing supplier remains unidentified and is a priority follow-up.

coverage_gaps.description: Group-parent newsrooms (Erste Group for Slovenska sporitelna, Intesa Sanpaolo for VUB, Raiffeisen Bank International for Tatra banka, KBC for CSOB) were not systematically searched; group-level vendor deals often cover the SK subsidiary without a SK-language announcement.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add group-parent press/IR newsrooms and their supplier announcements to the watchlist and re-run vendor-name queries scoped to those domains.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side press-release archives and newswires (vendor /news, /press, /newsroom subtrees; SK PR wires such as TASR/SITA business services) were only sampled, not enumerated. These typically carry the win announcement months before a polished case study exists.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate /novinky, /press, /newsroom paths for every vendor on the watchlist and set up keyword-filtered polling on SK PR wires.

coverage_gaps.description: Professional-network and job-market signals (vendor and bank hiring for named platforms, consultancy staffing for regulatory-reporting programmes) were not covered; these often reveal a platform choice before any announcement.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess LinkedIn/Profesia job-posting monitoring for platform names at SK banks and their integrators, and record access/legal constraints before collecting.

coverage_gaps.description: Big-4 and consultancy SK practice pages (KPMG SK, Deloitte CZ/SK, PwC, EY) publish DORA/NIS2/regulatory-readiness material for the SK market and are themselves compliance-service vendors to banks, but were not profiled as sources in this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add SK-market consultancy insight pages as a distinct source subtype (advisory vendor content), which doubles as a deadline/consultation tracker and a vendor-positioning signal.

coverage_gaps.description: All candidate URLs in this slice were identified via search-result metadata and summaries; none were independently fetched and confirmed by this agent, and several (Tempest http-only, FinStat paid tiers) may have access constraints.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness/robots/ToS pass over every URL here before scheduling collection; re-check the Tempest legacy URL for an https/CMS replacement.

brief: For Slovak systemic banks, which are private and therefore outside public procurement portals, the only reliable published trace of compliance-driven buying is vendor-side: Slovak software houses (SOFTEC, AXASOFT, Asseco Central Europe, EEA, Goldmann Systems, ANASOFT, DATALAN, TEMPEST, NFQES) publish named 'referencie' and project case studies covering digital onboarding, branch systems, credit workflows and payment platforms at Tatra banka, Slovenska sporitelna, VUB, CSOB, Raiffeisen and 365.bank. These are complemented by SK tech press-release wires (TOUCHIT/BrandIT), financial trade press (FinReport), and event/association rosters (Slovak Fintech, Finweek, IBV NBS FinNext) that expose vendor-bank pairings before case studies appear. Regulator case files (EC merger cases such as M.10378, Protimonopolny urad decisions) are the strongest indirect route, since they describe shared infrastructure and supplier relationships the parties would not otherwise publish. The main blind spots are global vendors' SK wins (likely announced only via group parents Erste/Intesa/RBI/KBC), unannounced AML/KYC platform selections, and the unnamed implementer behind the joint instant-payments programme.
